html:
A mudslide and flood on the morning of 14 August 2017, when part of Sugar Loaf mountain above Freetown collapsed after days of heavy rain, burying homes in the Regent area.

More than a thousand people died, many asleep, and thousands lost their homes. Freetown had grown fast since the civil war, as people fled the countryside and built on the steep, cleared slopes around the city with little planning. The disaster came only a year after the end of the Ebola epidemic, which had killed nearly 4,000 Sierra Leoneans. It led to calls to stop building on the hills, which are still being settled.
sum: A mudslide and flood on the morning of 14 August 2017, when part of Sugar Loaf mountain above Freetown collapsed after days of heavy rain, burying homes in the Regent area.
